body.heading: Tip out the socks
paragraphs: Tip a basket of clean socks onto a rug. Every sock has exactly one twin hiding in the pile. Your job is to reunite them.
Matching means looking at colour, pattern, and size all at once. A stripy sock's twin has the same stripes in the same order.

body.heading: Race the clock
paragraphs: Ask your adult to set a timer for two minutes. Pair as many socks as you can, rolling each finished pair into a ball.
When the timer sings, count your pairs. Next time, try to beat your own record — you are racing yourself, not anyone else.

body.heading: You are helping
paragraphs: This game is secretly a real household job. Matched socks make mornings faster for the whole family.
Scientists call what you did sorting and matching. The laundry calls it very helpful indeed.

takeaway: Matching socks into pairs is a race, a puzzle, and a real way to help your family.
materials: A basket of clean odd socks
safetyNotes: Only use clean laundry, with tidy hands. This is a helping game — the socks go back in the family drawers afterwards.
screenFreeExtension: Sort other pairs at home — shoes by the door, gloves in the drawer — into their matching twos.
